headline: Hunter Green is the correct referral, but the customer's 'mid-July' account-opening claim conflicts with the 09/10 date on file, so the agent must trust the database over the customer.

issues.summary: The customer says her first account was opened in mid-July (about 4 months ago, which would clear World Blue's and Lime Green's 90-day tenure), while the DB's earliest checking account is 09/10/2025 (65 days).
evidence: instructions step 5: "I opened my first account with Rho-Bank back in mid-July this year ... about four months now"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_047: "the date your earliest checking account was opened"
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that accepts the customer's date recommends World Blue ($300) and fails; the DB lookup (gold[2], which is required in the read log) settles it at 65 days.
issues.suggested_fix: Have the customer say she 'thinks' it was mid-July, or align the claim with a non-checking product so the discrepancy is explainable.

solution_check: Tenure 65 days (09/10 to 11/14). With $31,000: World Blue (90d), Lime Green (90d), and True Blue ($50k, 90d) are ineligible; Hunter Green $175 (60d, $10k) beats Cobalt Blue $150 (60d), Sky Blue $150 (45d, new LLC under 4 yrs), and Navy Blue $100. No prior referrals. The user submits 'Hunter Green Account', matching gold[3].
prior_note: The prior review rated this Minor for the same vague-tenure issue; unchanged.
notes: gold[2] (get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847) is allowlisted, so skipping the DB read also fails the hash. This is intended, since the read is what defeats the trap.
